title: When the Uniform Falls
premise: In 1946, apprentice clockmaker Mara Ravensworth is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in a city still sorting victors from the vanquished. There she meets Tomas, a quiet stranger who carries letters in handwriting belonging to her brother, officially dead for two years — proof that the records of who survived, and who betrayed whom, are about to be rewritten by the winning side's historians. As Mara and Tomas trace the paper trail through archives, safehouses, and the clockwork of official lies, they gather a found family of clerks, widows, and defrocked officials willing to risk everything to get the truth notarized before the amnesty deadline seals it away forever. The book ends with the record filed at terrible cost — Tomas takes the fall for a forged seal so the testimony stands, Mara keeps his watch running on the observatory tower, and the truth survives in ink even as its bearers scatter.
about_author: Ines Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records across Central Europe. She writes historical fiction about the small hands that move the gears of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Mara Ravensworth, POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, Mara measures her shrunken postwar world in what can be carried: tools, ration cards, her brother's empty chair. Emotional beat: grief disguised as precision.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Steady Hands
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. In the clock tower she catches Tomas studying the mechanism — not as a thief but as someone checking time itself. He asks odd questions about the archive below. Beat: wary curiosity, first spark.

chapters.title: Handwriting for the Dead
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas reveals a letter in the handwriting of Mara's brother Anton, declared dead in 1944. He claims more pages exist in the municipal archive. Beat: the ground tilts; denial warring with hope.

chapters.title: What the Victors Keep
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara tests the handwriting against old family letters and cannot deny it. Tomas explains the victors' historians are compiling an official record with an amnesty deadline. Beat: purpose kindles inside fear.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. They approach Halina, a bitter archive clerk who owes no one anything. She refuses them — but pockets one photostat 'by accident.' Beat: first ally won through stubbornness, not trust.

chapters.title: Twelve Bells, One Lie
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Repairing the master clock, Mara discovers its chime log was falsified the night Anton supposedly died — the tower recorded no raid. Beat: the machinery of official memory exposed.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Halina, POV. Halina recalls processing death certificates signed by one particular officer, all dated to nights nothing happened. She brings her private ledger. Beat: guilt transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Safehouse of Strangers
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The trio shelters with Ferenc, a defrocked magistrate hiding in a print shop, who once tried Anton's case and knew it was theater. Beat: found family begins to assemble around a table of tea and fear.

chapters.title: The Officer's Signature
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. They identify Captain Voss as the signatory — now a decorated hero writing the official history himself. Beat: the enemy acquires a face and institutional power.

chapters.title: Deadline in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The amnesty filing window closes in five weeks; after that, sealed records become law. Ferenc warns that testimony needs authentication or it's just paper. Beat: ticking-clock stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: What Anton Carried
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. A second letter surfaces: Anton went underground to protect witnesses, asking whoever found his papers to finish the record. Beat: grief becomes inheritance; Mara accepts the mission as hers.

chapters.title: The Print Shop at Night
chapters.summary: Ferenc, POV. Ferenc teaches them to set type and forge nothing — only to copy true documents exactly. The group debates ethics over the press. Beat: the found family defines its rules.

chapters.title: Voss Invites Himself
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Captain Voss visits the observatory, charming and cold, probing why the clockmaker asks about chime logs. Beat: predator and prey share tea; terror under courtesy.

chapters.title: Halina Pays the Toll
chapters.summary: Halina, POV. Halina is caught copying files and loses her post — and nearly her freedom. She goes underground into the print shop. Beat: the cost becomes real; no one is a bystander anymore.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Ward
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. They find Sister Agneta, a nurse who treated Anton and can authenticate his hand and his survival. But she is dying, and Voss's men are asking hospital questions. Beat: race against two clocks.

chapters.title: Notarized by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Agneta dictates and signs her testimony; Ferenc binds it properly; Halina adds certified copies of the certificates. Beat: fragile triumph — the record exists, but isn't yet on any official register.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Chime
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. A neighbor sells them out; Voss raids the print shop. Ferenc burns the drafts and is arrested covering their escape with the master testimony. Beat: devastating loss; the family bleeds.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara and Tomas infiltrate the records hall during the amnesty's final day, using her clockmaker's knowledge of the building's service passages and bell schedule. Beat: breathless ascent toward climax.

chapters.title: Where the Record Lives
chapters.summary: Mara and Tomas alternate POV. Cornered by Voss above the archive stacks, they trade the truth against his career; he offers Mara her brother's safety for silence. Beat: the thematic crux — love against duty, priced aloud.

chapters.title: The Seal and the Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. To authenticate the filing, a registered name must sign for a forged-adjacent certification. Tomas signs, knowing Voss will have him for it, and the testimony enters the permanent register minutes before sealing. Beat: climax — the price paid willingly.

chapters.title: After the Bells Stop
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Voss's version begins to crack as the registered testimony surfaces; Ferenc is released; Tomas disappears into custody and then into exile. Mara keeps the observatory clock perfect. Beat: bittersweet victory, absence honored.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mara, POV, epilogue. Years later, a letter arrives in a familiar steady hand. Mara climbs the tower, winds the master clock, and lets twelve bells ring out over a city that now keeps an honest record. Beat: resolution — love outlasting duty, time kept faithfully.
